english.title: Make a statement known to be misleading/false/deceptive in purported compliance with an information notice - aggravated
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having been given a notice under

(A)_[section 12]_
(B)_[section 13]_

of the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022, in purported compliance with that notice, made a statement that was misleading, false or deceptive in a material particular, namely **(..SPECIFY STATEMENT..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 15B of the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
having been given a notice under section 12/13
in purported compliance with the notice
made a statement
known to be misleading/false/deceptive
in a material particular

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: This is the aggravated form of the offence which is committed when a person makes a statement that they know to be misleading, false or deceptive. For the basic form of this offence see H101610.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine. The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court and may be 6 or 12 months depending on the date of conviction, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
